title: Sum of Digits
directAnswer: Loop while `n > 0`: add `n % 10` to a running total, then do `n /= 10`. The `% 10`/`/ 10` pair is the digit-extraction idiom.

remember.takeaway: `% 10` then `/ 10` is the two-line idiom behind reverse, sum, and palindrome of digits.
remember.formula: total=0; while n>0: total += n%10; n//=10
whenToUse: Aggregating something over a number's digits

problemStatement: Given a non-negative integer `n`, return the sum of its digits.
understanding: Peel off the last digit with `% 10`, add it, then drop it with `/ 10`, until nothing is left.

approaches.name: Modulo and divide
approaches.whenToMention: This is the standard, expected solution — lead with it.
approaches.explanation:
Peel digits off the right with `% 10`, add each to a running total, then drop it with `/ 10`, until the number is exhausted. Seeding the total at 0 makes n = 0 correct for free.

**Why the order matters.** You must *read* the digit (`n % 10`) before you *remove* it (`n /= 10`). Swap the two and you'd divide first, lose the digit, and sum the wrong values. The standard idiom is `total += n % 10; n /= 10;` in that order.

**Why the loop terminates.** Integer division by 10 strictly shrinks any positive number toward 0, so `while (n > 0)` always ends. Using `>=` instead would loop forever once n hits 0 (0 / 10 stays 0).

This `% 10` / `/ 10` pair is the single most reused idiom across digit problems — reverse, palindrome, Armstrong, and digital-root all lean on it.
hints: How do you read just the last digit of a number? How do you remove it?
`n % 10` is the last digit; `n / 10` drops it. Add then drop.
Loop while `n > 0`, seeding the total at 0.
approaches.complexityReasoning: one modulo and one division per digit — proportional to the digit count.

dryRun.intro: Add the last digit, then strip it.

edgeCases.behavior: Loop body never runs; the seed 0 is returned.
Sums to 1; only one non-zero digit.

pitfalls: Dividing before reading the digit, so you sum the wrong values.
Using `n >= 0` as the loop guard and never terminating.

commonMistakes: Swapping the order so you divide before reading the digit.

followupVariations.title: Add Digits (digital root)
followupVariations.hint: Repeat digit-sum until one digit remains; or use the 1 + (n−1) % 9 formula.

followupVariations.title: Happy Number
followupVariations.hint: Sum of squared digits, looped with cycle detection.

patternNote: A core fresher pattern: Digit extraction (`%10`, `/10`). Master it on small inputs and it transfers to harder problems.

interviewerIntent.testing: Whether you apply the read-then-strip digit idiom in the correct order with a terminating loop.
interviewerIntent.commonMistake: Reversing the modulo/divide order, or an infinite loop from a `>= 0` guard.
interviewerIntent.toStandOut: Note that repeatedly summing digits gives the digital root, a common follow-up.
